title: Unit 16 Gases (part 4)
textbookText: The balanced chemical equation involved in the laboratory preparation of ammonia gas is 2NH₄Cl(s) + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCl₂ (s) + 2H₂O (l) + 2NH₃(g). 5 Observe the given diagram and answer the following questions. i) Which gas is prepared by using given apparatus? Write balanced chemical reaction occurred in that process. Ans:- Carbon dioxide gas is prepared by using given apparatus. The balanced chemical equation involved in that process is CaCO₃ (s) + 2HCl (aq) → CaCl₂ (aq) + H₂O (l) + CO₂ (g). ii) Write the name of compound formed when that gas is dissolved in water. Ans:- When carbon dioxide gas is dissolved in water, it forms carbonic acid (H₂CO₃). iii) How can we test that gas in the laboratory? Ans:- Carbon dioxide gas can be tested in the laboratory by passing it through lime water (Ca(OH)₂ solution); if the lime water turns milky, it confirms the presence of carbon dioxide. iv) Write one use of that gas. Ans:- Plants use carbon dioxide as a raw material for the preparation of their food. 6. Draw a diagram of laboratory preparation of ammonia gas and label any four parts. Why this gas cannot be collected in the gas jar by downward displacement of water? Ans:- The labelled diagram of laboratory preparation of ammonia gas is given below, Ammonia gas cannot be collected by the downward displacement of water because it is highly soluble in water and reacts with it to form a solution, rather than displacing it to fill the jar. 7. In a practical exam, you have been given egg shell, hydrochloric acid, conical flask, thistle funnel, cork, delivery tube, gas jar and litmus paper. Which gas can you prepare by using these materials? Draw a well labelled diagram of your experiment. Ans:- Eggshells are primarily composed of Calcium Carbonate CaCO₃. So I can prepare carbon dioxide by using these materials. To prepare the gas, place the crushed eggshells as a calcium carbonate in a conical flask. Fit the flask with a cork containing two holes: one for the thistle funnel (to add acid) and one for the delivery tube. The gas is collected in a gas jar by the upward displacement of air because carbon dioxide is heavier than air. You can test the gas using moist blue litmus paper, which will turn red, indicating the gas is acidic.

8. The alphabets in the following chemical reaction do not represent the actual symbols of the elements. ABC3 ∆⃗ AC + BC2 If compound AC is used to remove the acidity of soil, answer the following questions. i) If the gas BC2 is produced even when ABC3 reacts with HCl, name the compound ABC3 and write the balanced chemical reaction. (Ans: ABC3= CaCO3) Ans:- If the gas BC2 is produced even when ABC3 reacts with HCl, The name of the compound ABC3 is CaCO3 and the balanced chemical reaction between CaCO3 and HCl is CaCO3 + 2HCl → CaCl₂ (aq) + H₂O (l) + CO₂ (g). ii) Rewrite the above chemical reaction with correct symbols of the elements.
∆ Ans:- The above chemical reaction with correct symbols of the elements is CaCO3 → CaO + CO₂. iii) What is formed when the gas so produced reacts with water? Write it's the chemical reaction.

Ans:- When the gas produced (CO₂) reacts with water, it forms a weak acid called Carbonic acid and its chemical reaction is CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO3. 9. A farmer is suggested to use the solid compound obtained after heating calcium carbonate in his/her field. Answer the following question based on this short piece of information: i) State, with a suitable reason, the problem of the farmer. Ans:- When calcium carbonate (CaCO3) is heated, it undergoes thermal decomposition to produce calcium oxide (CaO), also ∆ know as quicklime and carbon dioxide gas. CaCO3 → CaO + CO₂. Based on that the farmer’s problem is that the soil in the field is too acidic because soil acidity can occur due to heavy rainfall ( leaching of minerals), excessive use of chemical fertilizers or the decay of organic matter. Acidic soil is harmful because it reduces the availability of essential nutrients and can make toxic elements like aluminum more soluble which stunts plant growth. ii) How does the use of given compound help to solve her/his problem? Explain with a suitable chemical reaction.
Ans:- The solid compound obtained is Calcium Oxide (CaO). When this is added to the field, it reacts with the moisture (water) in the soil to form Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂) which is a strong base.

Chemical reaction involved in reaction with soil moisture is CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ The resulting calcium hydroxide neutralizes the acids present in the soil. The hydroxide ions (𝑂𝐻−) from the base react with the hydrogen ions (𝐻+) form the acidic soil to form water, thereby raising the soil pH to a neutral or slightly alkaline level suitable for crops. Chemical reaction involved in this process is Ca(OH)₂ + 2𝐻+ (from acidic soil) → 𝐶𝑎++ + 2H₂O.
